title: A topic plan
context: A first draft of the topics for the house, and the filter a dashboard uses to show every temperature.
code:
# published by devices
/Home/Kitchen/fridge temp      4.2
home/kitchen/fridge/temp/4.2
home/hall/light               toggle

# the dashboard subscribes to
home/+/temp

findings.t: The value is in the topic
findings.d: `home/kitchen/fridge/temp/4.2` makes a new topic per reading, so nothing can subscribe to "the fridge's temp" or retain it. Topic `home/kitchen/fridge/temp`, payload `4.2`.

findings.t: Leading slash, capitals and a space
findings.d: `/Home/Kitchen/fridge temp` has an empty first level (so `home/#` never matches it), differs by case from `home/...`, and NATS refuses the space. All lower-case, no leading slash, no spaces.

findings.t: The dashboard's filter matches nothing here
findings.d: `home/+/temp` is three levels; the temps are four (`home/<room>/<device>/temp`). `home/+/+/temp`.

findings.t: A command on the state topic, as a toggle
findings.d: `home/hall/light toggle` mixes a command with the light's state, and a repeated toggle undoes itself. `home/hall/light/power/set ON`, and the light reports on `home/hall/light/power`.

title: A paho subscriber
context: Logs the kitchen's readings. It works on the desk; after a day on the Pi it has stopped logging, with no error.
code:
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

def on_message(client, userdata, msg):
    if msg.payload == "OPEN":
        notify("fridge door open")
    log_reading(msg.topic, float(msg.payload))

client = mqtt.Client(mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2, client_id="logger")
client.on_message = on_message
client.connect("jarvis", 1883)
client.subscribe("home/kitchen/#")
client.loop_forever()

findings.d: After the first reconnect (Wi-Fi blip, broker restart) the clean session has no subscriptions and the client receives nothing, silently. Subscribe in `on_connect`, which runs on every connect.

`home/kitchen/#` also matches `.../status` ("online") and the door's "OPEN". The ValueError escapes the callback, and by default paho re-raises it out of `loop_forever()`, ending the program. Dispatch on the topic; catch and log bad payloads.
The payload is bytes. `msg.payload == b"OPEN"`, or decode first.
`logger` is likely to be used by another program too; the two evict each other. Make it unique: `kitchen-logger-jarvis`.
`subscribe` without `qos=` is QoS 0, so door events can be lost. `qos=1` for events.

title: Online and offline
context: A sensor's status topic, so the dashboard can show which devices are up.
code:
client = mqtt.Client(mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2, client_id="fridge-a4cf12")
client.connect("jarvis", 1883, keepalive=60)
client.will_set("home/kitchen/fridge/status", "offline", qos=1)
client.publish("home/kitchen/fridge/status", "online", qos=1, retain=True)
client.loop_start()
...
# on shutdown
client.disconnect()

findings.d: The will is part of CONNECT; set after it, it's never sent to the broker, so a crash leaves "online". Call `will_set` before `connect`.
Even when set right, a non-retained "offline" reaches only current subscribers; the retained "online" stays the topic's value. `retain=True` on the will.

findings.t: A clean shutdown never says offline
findings.d: `disconnect()` discards the will. Publish "offline" (retained) and wait for it before disconnecting.

findings.t: "online" is published once, not per connect
findings.d: After a reconnect the broker has already published the will "offline" (if the drop was unclean). Publish "online" in `on_connect`, every time.

title: An aiomqtt service
context: Inside a FastAPI app: listens for the washing machine's power readings and lets a route turn the plug off.
code:
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app):
    asyncio.create_task(listen())
    yield

async def listen():
    async with aiomqtt.Client("jarvis", identifier="house-api") as client:
        await client.subscribe("tele/washer/SENSOR")
        async for m in client.messages:
            data = json.loads(m.payload)
            requests.post(FRIDAY, json={"power": data["ENERGY"]["Power"]})

@app.post("/washer/off")
async def washer_off():
    async with aiomqtt.Client("jarvis", identifier="house-api") as c:
        await c.publish("cmnd/washer/POWER", "OFF")

findings.t: The route and the listener share a client ID
findings.d: Each POST connects as `house-api`, evicting the listener, whose `async for` then raises and (see next) never comes back. Keep one client from the lifespan and publish through it.
When the connection drops, `MqttError` ends `listen()` and the task dies silently: no more readings until a restart. Wrap it in `while True` with try/except MqttError and backoff, subscribing inside.
Every reading stalls the whole app, every route and the MQTT keepalive, for the length of an HTTP call. `await` an `httpx.AsyncClient` (from the lifespan).

findings.t: The task isn't kept or cancelled
findings.d: `create_task` without keeping a reference can be garbage-collected, and nothing cancels it at shutdown. `task = ...`, `task.cancel()` after `yield`.
Tasmota sends a reading every TelePeriod; this notifies Friday each time. Detect the transition (running to done) and notify once.

title: A heater schedule
context: Turns the hall heater off at night.

findings.d: Every time the heater reconnects (every reboot, every Wi-Fi blip) it gets the retained message and acts again, days later. Commands are never retained.
Sent twice, or replayed, it turns the heater back on. Send the target state: `OFF`.

findings.t: On the state topic, not a command topic
findings.d: `home/hall/heater/power` is where the heater reports; publish to `home/hall/heater/power/set`.
If the heater is offline for a moment, the command is lost. QoS 1, with a persistent session on the heater.

title: Switching MQTT on, on jarvis
context: A first attempt at the leaf's config, so devices can connect.

findings.d: NATS checks the converted subject: `home.kitchen.fridge.>` (and `home.kitchen.fridge` for the `#` subscribe). As written, every publish and subscribe is refused.

findings.t: A plain-text password in the config
findings.d: The config is in the Nix store, world-readable, and in git. Use a bcrypt hash from `nats server passwd`, as the VPS does.

findings.t: Local programs now need a login
findings.d: Adding `authorization` makes the 127.0.0.1 client port require one too, and today's local programs send none. Plan for it (a `no_auth_user` for local programs, or logins for each).
The fridge's login works on the NATS client port too. Limit device users to `["MQTT"]`.

findings.t: No `js_domain: home` in the mqtt block
findings.d: Say where MQTT's state lives, so sessions and retained values stay on the Pi and the house works without the hub.

title: A wake-up command from NATS
context: A nats-py job on the VPS tells the battery-powered pantry scale, which sleeps and wakes every 10 minutes, to tare itself.
code:
nc = await nats.connect("nats://100.64.0.21:4222", user="pantry", password=PW)
await nc.publish("home/pantry/scale/tare", b"now")
await nc.close()

findings.t: From NATS, MQTT subscribers get QoS 0
findings.d: The scale is asleep, so the message isn't queued for it, persistent session or not. Publish over MQTT at QoS 1 to the leaf, or keep the request in a stream and have the scale ask on wake.

findings.t: The subject is written as an MQTT topic
findings.d: `home/pantry/scale/tare` is one NATS token that happens to contain slashes. The scale's MQTT subscription to `home/pantry/scale/tare` is the subject `home.pantry.scale.tare`, so this never matches it.
Arriving 10 minutes late, "now" is wrong. Send an id and a timestamp, so the scale can drop a stale request and ignore a repeat.

title: Mosquitto for a friend's flat
context: A friend's Mosquitto setup, port-forwarded so their phone works away from home.
code:
listener 1883 0.0.0.0
allow_anonymous true

# acl_file /etc/mosquitto/acl
# user devices
# topic readwrite #

findings.t: Anonymous, and open to the internet
findings.d: Anyone who scans the port can read every topic and drive every device. `allow_anonymous false`, a password file, and no port-forward: reach it over a VPN or Tailscale.

findings.t: No TLS on a port that leaves the house
findings.d: Passwords and payloads cross the internet in clear. If it must be reachable, 8883 with TLS; better not at all.
Every device would share one login with access to everything. A user per device, limited to its own topics.

title: Home Assistant discovery
context: A Python script announces its "washing done" sensor to Home Assistant at startup.

findings.d: Home Assistant only sees it if it happens to be running at that moment; after its next restart the sensor is gone. `retain=True`, and republish on `homeassistant/status` "online".
Without it the entity can't be renamed or managed in Home Assistant, and a second announcement can duplicate it.
It's an event. Retained, every Home Assistant restart sees "done" again, and automations fire. Retain it only if you also publish OFF when the next wash starts, or don't retain it.
If the script dies, the sensor keeps its last value. Add `availability_topic` with a retained will "offline".

title: Door notifications
context: Notifies Friday when the front door opens. Zigbee2MQTT publishes `{"contact": false}` for open.
code:
last = None

async def handle(topic, payload):
    global last
    data = json.loads(payload)
    if data["contact"] == False and last != False:
        await notify("Front door opened")
    last = data["contact"]

async def run():
    async with aiomqtt.Client("jarvis", identifier="door", clean_session=False) as c:
        await c.subscribe("zigbee2mqtt/#", qos=1)
        async for m in c.messages:
            await handle(m.topic.value, m.payload)

findings.d: It subscribes to `zigbee2mqtt/#`, so any device's message (a lamp, the bridge) updates `last` or raises KeyError. Subscribe to the door's topic, and keep the last value per topic.
`zigbee2mqtt/bridge/state` and other devices have no `contact`. The exception ends the `async for`, and there's no reconnect loop to restart it. `.get()`, and catch per message.

findings.t: A retained or queued "open" at start notifies
findings.d: On restart, `last` is None; the retained state or messages queued in the persistent session arrive and "Front door opened" fires for an old event. Skip retained messages (`m.retain`) and old timestamps.
A bouncing contact sends open-closed-open in a moment: two notifications. Ignore a second open within a few seconds.

findings.t: Persistent session under a generic ID
findings.d: `door` is easy to reuse elsewhere; with clean_session off, a collision also mixes up queued messages. A unique, stable ID.

title: Reliable by decree
context: "We need every door event, so the sensor publishes at QoS 2."
code:
sensor:     publish  home/hall/door/contact  qos=2
logger:     subscribe home/hall/door/#       qos=0   clean_session=True
handler:    db.insert(event)        # on every message

findings.t: The subscription caps it at QoS 0
findings.d: Delivery is at the lower of publish and subscribe QoS: the logger gets QoS 0, fire and forget. Subscribe at QoS 1.

findings.t: A clean session loses events while the logger is down
findings.d: During a restart or a deploy nothing is kept for it. Persistent session with a stable client ID.
At QoS 1, repeats happen. Insert keyed by an event id or timestamp from the payload, ignoring one already stored.

findings.t: QoS 2 from the sensor costs without helping
findings.d: Four packets per event on a small device, for a guarantee the subscriber throws away. QoS 1 plus an idempotent handler.
